QF.id: AIFM CII Legal Documents and Negotiations_3

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah is counsel to 'Ganga Infra Trust AIF', a Category I AIF launching its third scheme. The sponsor asks whether a fresh Investment Management Agreement must be signed for each new scheme. What is the correct position?

answer.text: A fresh IMA must be signed for each scheme along with filing with SEBI 30 days prior.
The IMA is signed once for the trust as a whole and is not signed again at the launch of each scheme.
The IMA must be renewed every financial year through an addendum filed with the merchant banker.
The IMA is signed only for the first scheme and a Memorandum of Understanding suffices for subsequent schemes.

explanation.text: The Logic: The IMA is entered into between the trustee (on behalf of the AIF) and the investment manager once at the trust level, and governs the delegation of management powers for the AIF as a whole. It is not re-signed at the launch of each scheme — each new scheme is on-boarded through the PPM filing process. The Trap: The '30 days prior' and merchant-banker concept belong to PPM filing, not the IMA. No annual renewal or MoU substitute is recognised under the AIF Regulations. Note: Workbook pages 102 and 180 confirm the trust-level IMA structure and frequency; page 187 supports new-scheme PPM filing as the operative on-boarding step.
